Integrate $\frac{dy}{dx} = 12(2x + 1)^{-2}$ using the reverse chain rule:
$$y = \int 12(2x + 1)^{-2}\,dx = \frac{12(2x + 1)^{-1}}{-1 \times 2} + c = -\frac{6}{2x + 1} + c$$

Substitute the given point $(1, 1)$ to find the integration constant $c$:
$$1 = -\frac{6}{2(1) + 1} + c \implies 1 = -\frac{6}{3} + c = -2 + c \implies c = 3$$
$$y = 3 - \frac{6}{2x + 1}$$

Find the $x$-intercept by setting $y = 0$:
$$3 - \frac{6}{2x + 1} = 0 \implies \frac{6}{2x + 1} = 3 \implies 2x + 1 = 2 \implies x = \frac{1}{2}$$
$$\text{Intersection Point: } \left(\frac{1}{2}, \, 0\right)$$
